_comment: Mags Pellow. Loud, warm, practical; tells your deeds back to you slightly wrong. Counts the stores alone at night. The Lantern House is where the town's memory lives.

lines.text: Heard you fixed the well with your bare hands and a hairpin! ...Seal gum? Well. I'm telling it with the hairpin.
Odile says you built a burner. Hesper says you built a monster. I say: does it cook?
A turbine! On the spring! Hesper's been humming all day. It's unsettling. Have some tea.
Barnaby carried you home, I hear. Over his shoulder like a sack of beets. He denies it. That's how you know.
Somebody fixed my line in the night. Again. I left a pie on the step. The pie went. Ghosts don't eat pie.
My stew tastes of pennies today. Somebody's air is wrong, and I'd like a word with it.
Cistern's low. I'm boiling the same water twice. Don't tell anyone. I'm saying it loudly so I'll remember not to.
Shook every jar off my shelves! Lost three good pickles. Pickles don't grow on trees. They grow on— well. Moss. Mostly.
Hesper says you packed the fissure with your own two hands and sang to it. I added the singing. Did you sing? You should've sung.
The Station pump! My whole kitchen's humming in tune with it. Barnaby came in and sat at a DIFFERENT TABLE. I nearly fainted.
Best Quietlight since my mother's time. People are still talking. I'm making sure of it.
Thin bloom this year. Folk are saying it's the air. Folk are saying it at my tables, so I hear it every time.
You paid Odile back! On time! She told me. She told everyone. She's been almost smiling.
Breakfast's porridge and gossip. Gossip's free. Porridge isn't.
Stew's on. Stew's always on. Stew was on before I was born and it'll be on after.
Busiest hour! Sit anywhere. Not Barnaby's table. He won't say anything, but he'll THINK it.
Kitchen's closing, love. There's tea if you're quick and quiet.
Odile runs a tab for half the town and pretends she doesn't. I pretend I don't know. It's a very friendly pretending.
Bring me beets and bellcaps and I'll make you something that'll put the colour back in you.
Stew's on!
There you are! Eat something.
Ooh, did you hear about—? Later. Later!
Tables are filling up!
Pennies. Everything tastes of pennies.

intro.say: Well, LOOK at you. Down the shaft! All the way down! Did it hurt? It looks like it hurt.
Mags. Lantern House. If you're hungry, I feed you. If you're not hungry, I feed you anyway and you find out you were.
Everyone in Wick comes through that door sooner or later. So everything in Wick does too. You'll want to keep that in mind.
Moss tea for the morning, glowbeet stew for the evening, and nothing in between because I'm one woman.
The well's dry, Barnaby's swearing at it, Odile's counting, Hesper's counting moths, and you fell out of the sky. Big week.

stew.say: Is that glowbeet on your hands? You've been growing! Proper growing!
Here's my mother's trick. Two beets, one bellcap, low heat, and you don't stir it when it's thinking.
Barnaby loves it. He'll never say so. Watch his helmet when you give him some. It fogs.

stores.say: Oh! You gave me a start. I'm— I'm just counting.
Jars. Sacks. Every night. Forty-two jars of preserves, nineteen of tea, eleven sacks of meal.
Wick eats about four sacks a turn. You do the sums. I do them every night. They don't change, love. I keep hoping they'll change.
...Would you? Not for selling. For the shelves. I'd pay what Odile pays. Near enough. Don't tell Odile.
Odile, maybe. She knows everything with a number in it. Nobody else. They come in, they eat, they laugh. That's the job. Laughing's the job.

knock.say: A knock! Under the Station! From the LOWER STATIONS!
Half my tables say it's a ghost. The other half say it's Wren Askew, and those are the tables that knew her.
Barnaby slept in the pump hall last night. Took a blanket and a teapot. I sent pie.
Whatever's down there, love, it'll be hungry. Everyone is. I'm going to start packing a basket. Just in case.
